content.title: About
content.content: Almond Chicken is a dish where bite‑size pieces of chicken breast are first sautéed and then simmered in a sauce made with ground almonds, soy sauce, honey, and spices. The almonds give the dish a subtle nutty aroma and a pleasant crunch, while the chicken provides lean protein and juiciness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Almonds are a common ingredient in both Asian and Mediterranean cuisines.
Traditional recipes use whole or ground almonds, but they can be swapped for cashews or hazelnuts.
In Chinese cuisine the dish is known as "鸡仁杏仁" (ji ren xing ren).
Almonds add a light sweetness, so honey or brown sugar is often included.
The dish is quick to prepare: chicken browning takes 5‑7 minutes, and simmering in the sauce another 10‑12 minutes.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken breast supplies high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Healthy fats from almonds
items.content: Almonds provide monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both chicken and almonds contain B6 and B12, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Almonds contribute magnesium and iron, while chicken adds zinc and phosphorus.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Vitamin E from almonds helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Tree‑nut allergy
items.content: Almonds may trigger allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: The dish can be calorie‑rich due to nuts and oil, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce adds salt; those watching sodium intake should opt for low‑sodium soy sauce.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve almond chicken hot, typically over rice, noodles, or a vegetable side. Sprinkle extra toasted almond slices and fresh herbs for added texture and flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat gently with a splash of water or broth to prevent the sauce from drying out.
